region: Roman coast and Constantine, then Djanet and the Tassili n'Ajjer
title: Algeria — Roman Shores and the Tassili Galleries
subtitle: From the Casbah and Tipasa's seaside ruins to Neolithic rock art above Djanet, on a licensed Tuareg-guided plateau trek
summary: Roman and Numidian sites around Algiers and Constantine, then an agency-escorted desert camping trek on the Tassili n'Ajjer. Security status is conditional: the southern leg sits close to the Libyan border strip and follows a 2024 killing in Djanet and a 2025 kidnapping in the region.
introduction: Two weeks that run from the Mediterranean to the central Sahara. You start in Algiers' Casbah, drive west to Tipasa and Cherchell where Roman streets and a theatre sit above the sea, then fly east to Constantine, a Numidian citadel on a gorge, and the hill town of Tiddis. A night flight puts you in Djanet, where a Tuareg guide and cook take you up the Tassili n'Ajjer escarpment: four nights of camping among Saharan cypresses and sandstone towers, rock shelters painted 6,000 years ago, and dunes at dusk. Everything in the south is guided and escorted by rule, so this is a guided expedition rather than a road trip.

exceptional.vsOman: Oman is a self-drive, self-camping trip with freedom to change plans. Algeria reverses that: the north is flights and hired drivers, the Sahara is only possible with a licensed agency, a local guide and army-monitored routes. What replaces the autonomy is a Tuareg-run walking camp on a UNESCO plateau, closer to Saharan prehistory than any Omani dune camp.
exceptional.vsPackageTourism: Most foreign visitors to the Algerian south join fixed agency circuits. This design keeps the agency (it is mandatory) but pairs it with unscripted northern days by public flights and local drivers, and a rock-art plateau walk instead of a 4x4 dune circuit.
exceptional.vsPortfolio: No other destination combines Roman Mauretania, a Numidian gorge city and a Neolithic rock-art museum in the open air within one itinerary. Tunisia and Jordan offer Roman ruins and desert camps more easily, but Algeria's ruins are almost visitor-free.

duration.note: Day 1 and day 13 are international flights; Djanet legs use night flights, so days 6/7 and 12/13 are partial.

recommendedTravelWindow.rationale: Starts after Eid al-Fitr holidays (expected 9–10 March) and avoids Ramadan. Djanet normals are 27/11 °C in March versus 23/6 °C in February, so plateau nights are less cold. Spring wind and dust are more frequent than in winter.

februarySuitability.summary: Cold, clear desert nights (Djanet record low −3.6 °C) and good plateau walking, but Ramadan from about 8 February reduces restaurant opening, and a mid-February window leaves only a few days before it starts.

marchSuitability.summary: After Ramadan and Eid, with milder nights and comfortable days. Dust and sirocco-type winds are possible and can disrupt flights and visibility; Mediterranean north is still showery.

climate.regionNote: Djanet (1,035 m) NOAA 1991–2020 normals, via Wikipedia; Algiers coast figures are approximate regional norms. Tassili plateau (about 1,500–1,900 m) is several degrees colder than Djanet; this is a planning estimate, not a station figure.

february.rainfall: Djanet 0.8 mm; Algiers coast about 70–80 mm (wettest months of winter).
february.notes: Djanet mean daily min 6.3 °C, record low −3.6 °C; plateau nights can go below freezing.

march.rainfall: Djanet 2.1 mm; Algiers coast about 60–70 mm.
march.notes: Djanet mean max 27.2 °C, min 11.5 °C, record low 0.8 °C. Wind and dust more frequent in spring.

climate.snowAndMountainAccess: Not relevant for the route; plateau is dry. Tassili access is on foot via escarpment paths arranged by the guide.
climate.seaConditions: Not relevant: Mediterranean coast is only a sightseeing setting at Tipasa and Cherchell.
climate.airQuality: Algiers has traffic pollution; the Sahara is generally clean but spring dust events reduce visibility.
climate.wildlifeSeasonality: Saharan cypress (Cupressus dupreziana) is evergreen; desert wildlife is scarce and not seasonal in a way that affects the trip.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Ramadan
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Daytime closures of restaurants and shorter site hours in the north; March window avoids it.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Eid al-Fitr
holidaysAndFestivals.dates: ≈ 9–10 Mar 2027 (moon-sighting dependent), several days of holiday
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Domestic flights and hotels are busy around Eid; starting 14 March keeps clear of the peak.

climate.ramadan2027: Ramadan is expected 8 Feb – 9 Mar 2027. Recommended window starts on 14 March, after Eid. A February departure would overlap Ramadan from about the 8th: daytime restaurants closed, shorter site hours, guides fasting.
climate.tourismDemand: Southern Algeria is a niche market (about 47,000 foreign visitors in the 2025-26 southern season per a trade report); the north is almost free of foreign tourists. Djanet agencies are busiest October to March.
climate.flightPriceSeasonality: Transavia winter fares Paris Orly–Algiers were about €113–129 return in February/March 2027 on a comparison site; Air Algérie fares from CDG are higher and not verified. Domestic Algiers–Djanet flights are cheapest booked about six weeks ahead.

geography.summary: Mediterranean coast and Constantine's limestone gorge in the north; the Tassili n'Ajjer sandstone plateau and the Erg Admer dune sea around Djanet in the south-east Sahara.
geography.distinctive: The Tassili n'Ajjer is a 72,000 km² sandstone massif of eroded towers and arches with a rare relict woodland of Saharan cypress, some of the oldest living trees in the Sahara, above a town of oases.

landscapes.name: Tassili n'Ajjer plateau
landscapes.description: Wind-carved sandstone towers, arches and canyons at about 1,500–1,900 m above the Djanet oasis, with scattered Saharan cypress.

landscapes.name: Erg Admer
landscapes.description: Red-orange dunes at the foot of the escarpment, used for the final desert night.

landscapes.name: Constantine gorge
landscapes.description: Rhumel river gorge crossed by a chain of bridges below the old city.

landscapes.name: Tipasa coast
landscapes.description: Roman port town on a rocky Mediterranean headland west of Algiers.

culture.summary: Roman Mauretania and Numidia, Ottoman and French-era Algiers, Saharan Tuareg culture and the Tassili's prehistoric rock art. Culture in the south is meeting the Tuareg guides who run the trek rather than visiting a village.

culturalHighlights.name: Casbah of Algiers
culturalHighlights.description: Hillside Ottoman-era medina of stepped lanes, mosques and courtyard houses. Visit with a local guide; parts are in poor repair.

culturalHighlights.name: Tipasa and Cherchell
culturalHighlights.description: Tipasa's Punic-Roman port town and basilicas on the shore; Cherchell (ancient Caesarea, capital of Mauretania Caesariensis) has a Roman theatre, baths and a museum of mosaics and statuary.

culturalHighlights.name: Constantine (Cirta) and Tiddis
culturalHighlights.description: Constantine's old city and bridges over the Rhumel gorge, then the terraced Roman-era hill town of Tiddis about 30 km away.

culturalHighlights.name: Tassili n'Ajjer rock art
culturalHighlights.description: Painted shelters recording the Sahara's shift from savanna to desert, seen on foot with a Tuareg guide.

culturalHighlights.name: Djanet and Tuareg hospitality
culturalHighlights.description: Old ksar and oasis gardens of Djanet, bread baked in sand and tea at the camp, led by local guides.

adventureHighlights.name: Tassili plateau trek
adventureHighlights.description: Four nights camping on and below the plateau, 4–6 hours of walking a day on rocky paths, escarpment ascent and descent; guide, cook and army-monitored route are mandatory.

adventureHighlights.name: Erg Admer dune camp
adventureHighlights.description: Night camp in the dunes below the escarpment by 4x4 with driver; no self-driving.

adventureHighlights.name: Constantine gorge walk
adventureHighlights.description: Walking the Perregaux footbridge and the Rhumel gorge bridges.

signatureExperiences.title: Four nights on the Tassili plateau
signatureExperiences.description: Walk up the escarpment from Djanet, camp among Saharan cypress (Tamrit sector), visit painted shelters at Sefar and Jabbaren, and sleep under open sky.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Open-air prehistory: paintings of cattle herds, human figures and animals from when the Sahara was green, seen without crowds or barriers.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Book a licensed Algerian agency; the agency files the paperwork, supplies Tuareg guide, cook, porters, camp gear and escort, and the route is confirmed in writing. Fly Algiers–Djanet. Operators advertise from about €1,500–2,000 per person for 8 days including international flights; a local 5-day ground package is estimated lower.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Estimated ground package for 5 days (guide, 4x4, camp gear, desert meals); no agency quote obtained, see budget lines.

signatureExperiences.title: Tipasa and Cherchell Roman coast day
signatureExperiences.description: Roman Tipasa on its headland and Cherchell's theatre and museum, with a hired driver from Algiers.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Ruins with the sea behind them and few other visitors; two sites and a mausoleum within an easy day.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Hired car and driver from Algiers (about 70 km, 1 h 15 min to Tipasa; Cherchell a further 30 km). Stay in a guesthouse in Tipasa.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Driver share and entry fees, estimate

signatureExperiences.title: Constantine gorge and Tiddis
signatureExperiences.description: Cross the Rhumel gorge by its bridges and walk the old city, then visit Tiddis, a hill town with mosaics and cisterns.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: A dramatic city site and a rural Roman hill town that tour groups rarely reach.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Fly Algiers–Constantine (about 1 h); car and driver to Tiddis (about 30 km); Belgian advice prefers flights over road for northern city links.

signatureExperiences.title: Casbah of Algiers on foot
signatureExperiences.description: Half-day with a local guide through the Casbah's stairways, then the national museum if open.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: A living Ottoman medina on the Mediterranean, rarely included in itineraries.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Local guide through the hotel or agency; avoid photographing officials or police.

travelStyle.summary: Guided and escorted by regulation in the south; hired drivers and domestic flights in the north. No self-drive.

transport.summary: International flight to Algiers, then domestic flights to Constantine and Djanet (Air Algérie group; Domestic Airlines operates Algiers–Djanet from February 2026). Northern excursions use a hired car with driver; desert legs use agency 4x4 and walking.

modes.description: Paris CDG–Algiers about 2 h 25 min; Air Algérie from CDG, Transavia from Orly.
Algiers–Constantine about 1 h; Algiers–Djanet about 2 h 15 min, usually night departures, up to two a day, carry passports on domestic flights.

transport.carRental: Not recommended or used. Self-drive rental exists in the north but road conduct is hazardous, Belgian advice favours flights, and desert travel without a guide is not allowed. Rental terms were not verified.

drivingRequirements.summary: Self-driving in the Sahara is not possible without a guide. In the north it may be legal but is not recommended here, given high accident rates and frequent checkpoints.
drivingRequirements.internationalDrivingPermit: Not verified. A Dutch driving licence is stated valid by the Netherlands advisory; for other licence countries check an Algerian consulate before any rental.
drivingRequirements.licenceNotes: Two of the four hold car licences and could share driving if a rental were used, but the plan uses drivers.
drivingRequirements.motorcycleNotes: No motorcycle or scooter use. Alternatives are hired drivers, agency 4x4, domestic flights and walking.
drivingRequirements.recommendedApproach: Domestic flights plus hired car with driver in the north; agency 4x4 with driver in the south.

accommodation.summary: Hotels in Algiers and Constantine, a guesthouse in Tipasa, a lodge or guesthouse in Djanet, and agency tents on the plateau and in the dunes.

camping.summary: Camping is only through the agency in the Tassili and Erg Admer; independent camping is not an option. Tents, mats and meals are supplied; a winter-rated sleeping bag is needed.

physicalDifficulty.label: demanding
physicalDifficulty.summary: 4–6 hours of walking per day on rocky ground with escarpment climbs, cold nights and dry dust; no technical difficulty. Good ordinary fitness is needed; no mountaineering skills.

itinerary.summary: Roman coast and Constantine in the north (days 1–5), a buffer day and night flight south (day 6), then a five-day Tassili walking trek with Tuareg guides from Djanet and a last dune camp (days 7–12). Only the Djanet-area programme depends on a licensed agency.

security.summary: No official source puts Djanet or the Tassili plateau in an orange or red zone, but the southern leg sits close to the Libyan border strip, a tourist was killed in Djanet in October 2024, a Spanish tourist was kidnapped near Tamanrasset in January 2025, and the entire Sahara is subject to escort rules. The original Roman programme (Timgad, Djémila) was removed because France lists Batna and Sétif wilayas as orange. A21 (27 Nov 2026): the US places Illizi, Tamanrasset and areas near the eastern border at Level 4 (Do Not Travel) for terrorism and kidnapping, so the Saharan leg sits on the excluded side of conditional; only France (yellow, organised trips with escort) and the FCDO 30 km strip leave it open.
security.assessedRoute: Algiers, Tipaza province (Tipasa, Cherchell), Constantine and Tiddis, then Djanet, the Tassili n'Ajjer plateau (Tamrit–Sefar–Jabbaren circuit) and Erg Admer. Excluded from the design: Timgad (Batna wilaya), Djémila (Sétif wilaya), Aurès, Tadrart Rouge, Tin Merzouga, Essendilene and any travel near border strips.

advisories.level: Algiers and Oran green; Sahara around Tamanrasset yellow (vigilance renforcée); Batna, Sétif, Aïn Defla wilayas, Aurès, Chréa, Tindouf, Hassi Messaoud orange; border zones red; Illizi and Djanet not individually named
advisories.regionsAffected: Batna and Sétif wilayas; all land-border zones including Libya, Niger, Mali; Sahara requires guide and escort
advisories.routeImpact: Timgad and Djémila removed. Tassili and Djanet fall under the yellow Sahara regime (accredited agency, guide, army-monitored routes, escort). Border-strip width not stated.

advisories.level: Advise against all travel within 30 km of the Libya, Mauritania, Mali and Niger borders; all but essential within 30 km of the rest of the Tunisia border; Djanet and Tassili not named
advisories.routeImpact: Djanet is about 64 km from Libya by an approximate map calculation and is outside the strip; the Tassili circuit approaches it and needs a track check. FCDO also states a heightened risk of kidnap in remote desert areas, particularly the southern and eastern border areas (re-read 27 Nov 2026).

advisories.level: Yellow for the rest of Algeria; red within 50 km of the Libyan border and within 200 km of Mauritania, Mali and Niger borders; Djanet and Tamanrasset named as risk areas
advisories.regionsAffected: 50 km Libya strip, 200 km Niger/Mali/Mauritania strip
advisories.routeImpact: Djanet airport is about 210 km from Niger and about 64–85 km from Libya on an approximate map calculation; the Tamrit–Sefar–Jabbaren circuit lies at or near the 50 km Libya line and cannot be cleared from public sources.

advisories.level: Avoid all travel within 200 km of Mali, Mauritania and Niger borders and within 50 km of Libya; high degree of caution elsewhere
advisories.routeImpact: Same border-strip uncertainty as the Dutch advice.

advisories.level: Level 2 overall; Level 4 Do Not Travel for areas near the eastern and southern borders, Bordj Badji Mokhtar, Illizi, In Guezzam, In Salah, Tamanrasset, the Tebessa mountains and Tindouf, and for remote Sahara areas without an organised tour (updated 24 Aug 2026; data feed)
advisories.regionsAffected: Eastern (Libya) and southern border areas; Illizi and Tamanrasset; remote Sahara
advisories.routeImpact: Djanet wilaya is not named, but it belonged to Illizi until 2019 and the Tassili circuit lies near the eastern border: the Saharan leg is very probably inside the US Level 4 area. This is the strongest conflict in the official advice.

advisories.level: Classic Grand Sud circuits (Tamanrasset, Djanet) currently dangerous because of persistent terrorism risk; use agencies and obtain approval; avoid all southern border zones
advisories.routeImpact: Directly addresses Djanet; strongest wording found.

conflictRisk.note: No active war inside the route, but Libya, Niger and Mali instability and closed Libyan and Moroccan borders create spillover risk in border strips.

terrorismRisk.note: FCDO says attacks are likely and the threat is higher in the Sahara and border areas; a tourist was killed in a cafe in Djanet on 11 October 2024 (motive unclear in press reports). Northern cities have had no major attack for years.

kidnappingRisk.note: A Spanish tourist was kidnapped near Tamanrasset in January 2025 and taken to Mali, per Spanish press; France confirms kidnapping risk in border zones; FCDO and Canada flag remote and border areas.

regionalRestrictions: Independent travel in the Algerian Sahara is not permitted: licensed agency, guide and army-monitored routes with escort.
Tourist visa on arrival for southern trips requires an approved agency and a programme including at least one of 24 listed southern wilayas, valid up to 30 days.
Border strips: 30 km (UK), 50 km Libya and 200 km Niger/Mali/Mauritania (Netherlands, Canada).
Binoculars, drones and navigation equipment can be confiscated at customs; no photography of military, police or religious sites.
ordinaryRisks: Very high road accident rate and weak lane discipline.
Frequent checkpoints; mobile coverage patchy in the south.
Sandstorm and dust events in spring; cold desert nights.
security.medicalAccess: Good private clinics in Algiers; Djanet and the Tassili have only basic care, with distances of hours by 4x4 and evacuation by air from Djanet or Algiers; medical evacuation insurance is essential.
security.insuranceConsiderations: Travelling to a region with an official advisory against travel can invalidate cover (FCDO notes this). Confirm in writing that the policy covers the Sahara, trekking and medical evacuation.
security.reassessmentRequired: Re-check all advisories before booking and two weeks before departure. Reassess if: the agency's GPS route enters the 50 km Libyan strip or the 200 km Niger strip; any incident in Djanet or Tamanrasset; France or FCDO change Illizi or Djanet; Libya/Niger border conditions change; insurer declines cover. The route would then become excluded. Reclassify as excluded if the State Department confirms that its Level 4 for Illizi and the eastern border covers Djanet wilaya, or if any other authority names Djanet.

practicalRequirements.visa: A visa is required for French, British and Dutch passport holders. For tourists on a programme that includes southern wilayas via an approved agency, a visa on arrival (e.g. in Djanet) is possible, valid up to 30 days; operator quotes €145–180. Conditional on nationality: confirm with the Algerian consulate or the agency. The northern-only part follows the ordinary consular visa.
practicalRequirements.entry: Agency sends boarding authorisation (QR code); passport copy needed about 15 days before departure in one operator's conditions. Register with the foreigners office in the wilaya; declare cash of €1,000 or more (Dutch advice) or above €5,000 (UK page); no binoculars or drones.
